Header: Asperisporium caricae Black spot of papaya

Prevention: A. caricae is a fungus that cause black spot on fruits and leaves of papaya.
It is spread from tree to tree by wind and wind-driven rains
Initiate orchards hygienically using seedlings that are free from pathogens from
KALRO, JKUAT Prune the trees to reduce humidity and improve air circulation in the orchard
Avoid overhead irrigation which spreads the spores through splash
Ensure crop vigor and good health through fertilizer and manure application
Keep the orchard free of weeds to minimize alternative hosts to the pathogen
Avoid working in fields when plants are wet and work on infected areas last
Monitoring: Scout the farm regularly for initial small, black spots on fruits and underside of leaves.
Spots are sunken yellow on the upper leaf surface
The black spot pathogen is hyperparasitized by another fungus ( Cephalosporium sp.) showing a white fungal growth around affected spots in the later stages
Take action once spots are observed on plants since the disease spreads fast through dispersion of spores, by air and splash and compromise fruit quality
Direct Control: Practice field sanitation by removing and destroying (by burning) severely infected plant parts and plant debris to reduce disease inoculum on the farm
Disinfect farm tools between plants and farms (Use 50 ml
JIK in 1 litre of water), to prevent spread of the fungus
Trianum-P ( Trichoderma harzianum ) at a rate of 15g in 5L or
Trichotech ( Trichoderma asperellum ) at a rate of 2.5g in 20L of water
Restrictions: When using pesticides, wear protective gear
Follow instructions on the product label
Disinfect all farm tools by dipping in 10% jik solution at 50ml/ L of water for atleast 5 minutes
Always consult recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB)
Ensure proper coverage of leaves and fruits
U (unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use); PHI 14 days, REI 14 days, toxic to aquatic organisms
Ensure proper coverage of the plants.
U (Unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use).
Apply when disease is expected or 1st symptoms seen.
Repeat after 14 days until flowering is over; REI 1 day; PHI 7 days
